Hypothesis: We hypothesize that a next-generation nanoparticle-based drug delivery system, which is specifically engineered with high-affinity targeting ligands for hepatic stellate cells and optimized drug release profiles, can be employed to achieve a controlled enhancement of p62 phosphorylation. This localized increase in p62 phosphorylation will promote the selective binding and autophagic degradation of Keap1, leading to a precisely monitored and quantitatively controlled activation of Nrf2. By integrating cutting-edge omics analyses and high-resolution imaging, we will define real-time biomarkers to maintain Nrf2 activity within a strictly therapeutic window, thereby upregulating cytoprotective antioxidant genes and reducing oxidative stress. Ultimately, this system is anticipated to inhibit hepatic stellate cell activation and attenuate liver fibrosis, all while avoiding the systemic oncogenic risks associated with diffuse Nrf2 activation.
Abstract: In this study, we propose a refined therapeutic strategy for mitigating liver fibrosis by leveraging a next-generation nanoparticle-based drug delivery system that is precisely engineered for targeting hepatic stellate cells. Our approach enhances p62 phosphorylation in a controlled and localized manner, thereby promoting the selective autophagic degradation of Keap1. This, in turn, regulates the nuclear translocation of Nrf2, monitored in real time using integrated omics platforms and high-resolution imaging technologies. By quantitatively defining and continuously adjusting the therapeutic window of Nrf2 activation via dynamic biomarkers, our method upregulates cytoprotective antioxidant genes, reduces oxidative stress, and suppresses hepatic stellate cell activation. Concomitantly, advanced pharmacokinetic modeling and ligand-receptor engineering ensure that the nanoparticles are confined to hepatic stellate cells, thereby minimizing off-target effects and mitigating the oncogenic risks associated with systemic Nrf2 activation. This refined strategy integrates mechanistic precision with state-of-the-art monitoring to achieve targeted antifibrotic effects.
CausalChain: Oxidative stress in liver cells -> Nanoparticle targeting of hepatic stellate cells (via ligand-specific binding and quantitative pharmacokinetics) -> Enhanced and controlled p62 phosphorylation (using drug-loaded nanoparticles with fine-tuned release kinetics) -> p62 binds Keap1 -> Autophagic degradation of Keap1 -> Precisely monitored Nrf2 nuclear translocation (through real-time omics and high-resolution imaging feedback loops) -> Upregulation of cytoprotective antioxidant genes -> Suppression of hepatic stellate cell activation -> Attenuation of liver fibrosis
